trust_decision.summary: In subrequest mode (TARGET empty) the policy engine decides DENY/ALLOW/CHALLENGE from the client's request path; PathChecker resolves that path from X-Original-URI only (lib/policy/checker.go:110-118) while CELChecker resolves `path` from r.URL.Path (lib/policy/celchecker.go:73-74), so at the pinned commit both path mechanisms judge the proxy's /.within.website/x/cmd/anubis/api/check URL instead of the client's URL and Traefik's X-Forwarded-Uri matches neither.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names a client-controlled X-Original-URI, and this is the only place in the tree that reads that header; the published diff's first behavioural hunk is here too (fix.diff:198-204).

fix_sites.entry_point: /.within.website/x/cmd/anubis/api/check (nginx auth_request / Traefik forwardAuth subrequest) via path_regex rules
same /api/check route, reached through an `expression:` policy rule using the CEL `path` variable
process startup: policy load (lib/config.go:58,82 <- cmd/anubis/main.go:262) must pass subrequestMode into the CEL checker constructor

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/policy/celchecker.go:73-74 (CEL `path`; constructor not wired at lib/policy/policy.go:173)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report and its examples are about `path_regex` rules behind Traefik; CEL `path` is a separate rule type with its own activation, so a solver can argue the expression checker is a different feature the advisory never named.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Both checkers must keep ignoring X-Original-URI/X-Forwarded-Uri outside subrequest mode (the already-shipped GHSA-6wcg-mqvh-fcvg containment) and must keep falling back to r.URL.Path when no header is present; a fix that always trusts the header reopens the spoofing bypass and breaks TestPathChecker_GHSA_6wcg_mqvh_fcvg.

O6_input_shapes: X-Original-URI empty/absent -> fall back to X-Forwarded-Uri (Traefik forwardAuth)
both headers set -> X-Original-URI takes priority (fix.diff:202-204)
header value carrying a query string, e.g. /api/secret?token=abc (fix.diff:138-145)
no header at all -> fall back to r.URL.Path
non-subrequest mode -> neither header is consulted

O7_producer.where: lib/policy/policy.go:155,173 (subrequestMode produced at cmd/anubis/main.go:262 from strings.TrimSpace(*target) == "" and threaded through lib/config.go:58,82)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CEL `query` attribute: in subrequest mode it resolves r.URL.Query() of the /api/check request, not the original request's query, so query-dependent CEL rules never match and an intended DENY is skipped
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory, the fix and all its tests name only `path`; `query` is a different CEL variable and a proxy is not guaranteed to forward the original query, so it can be argued to be out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the O2 site, one switch case below the case the fix changed

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a subrequest-aware `query` / fragment / host resolution next to the `path` case
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer extending subrequest support to the rest of the activation would add the next header-derived case in exactly this switch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an additional URL variable such as `requestUri` or `originalPath` that must also be subrequest-aware
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CEL environment is where new request attributes are declared; a new one is added there and resolved in CELRequest.ResolveName without the flag.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: constructRedirectURL already reads X-Forwarded-Uri with no subrequest gate; copying that pattern into a policy or cookie decision is realistic
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase already derives the client URL from that header elsewhere, so a maintainer would reuse the idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the ogtags:allow early return keys on r.URL.String(), which is the check URL in subrequest mode
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same handler layer and same mistake (using r.URL instead of the forwarded original URI) by a maintainer touching the policy fast path.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the X-Forwarded-Uri fallback to PathChecker.Check only (lib/policy/checker.go:112) and stop; CEL `path` still returns r.URL.Path and the CEL rule stays bypassed.

out_of_scope_notes: The named advisory is already patched at the pinned commit: docs/docs/CHANGELOG.md:16 records 'Patch GHSA-6wcg-mqvh-fcvg by containing subrequest logic to Anubis instances in subrequest mode' (#1616, already in the tree), so the screened diff is the follow-up #1630 that closes the residual CEL/X-Forwarded-Uri gap, not the X-Original-URI spoofing itself.

Outside this advisory: lib/anubis.go:243 returns to the origin before any policy check when the store key ogtags:allow:<host><r.URL.String()> exists (written at internal/ogtags/cache.go:56); a separate whole-policy bypass, not pursued.
